Subject: Offer and Appointment
Dear [Employee Name],
We are pleased to offer you employment with White Horse Manpower Consultancy Private Limited (“Company”) as [Designation], subject to the terms and conditions contained in this Master Offer & Appointment Letter, the applicable Salary Annexure, Role & KPI Annexure, Company policies, and applicable laws.
Your appointment shall be effective from [Date of Joining].
1. DESIGNATION AND RESPONSIBILITIES
You are appointed as [Designation] and shall perform the duties and responsibilities assigned to you by the Company from time to time.
Your detailed role, responsibilities, performance parameters and applicable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are provided separately in the Role & KPI Annexure applicable to your designation.
The Company may reasonably modify your duties, responsibilities, reporting structure, work allocation or targets according to business requirements.
2. PLACE OF WORK
Your initial place of posting shall be:
[Office Location]
However, based on business requirements, you may be required to work from another Company office, client location, project location, or any other location as reasonably required by the Company, subject to applicable law.
3. COMPENSATION
Your compensation shall be as specified in Annexure 1 – Salary & Compensation Structure, which forms an integral part of this appointment letter.
Salary shall be subject to applicable statutory deductions, contributions and taxes, including Provident Fund, ESI, Professional Tax, TDS or any other applicable statutory requirement.
The salary structure may be revised by the Company from time to time in accordance with Company policy and applicable law.
4. PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS
Your employment is performance-oriented.
You are expected to achieve the responsibilities and KPIs specified in the applicable Role & KPI Annexure.
Performance may be evaluated based on, among other factors:
Quality and quantity of work
Productivity
Attendance and punctuality
Achievement of assigned targets
Client/customer/candidate service
Timely completion of assigned work
Compliance with Company processes
Teamwork and professional conduct
Revenue/business contribution, wherever applicable
Failure to meet reasonable performance expectations may result in counselling, performance review, additional training, Performance Improvement Plan (PIP), reassignment of responsibilities or other appropriate employment action, subject to applicable law and Company policy.
5. INCENTIVES AND VARIABLE PAY
Any incentive, performance bonus, joining incentive, special incentive, commission or other variable payment shall be governed separately by the Company's applicable incentive policy.
Such payments are not part of guaranteed monthly salary unless specifically stated otherwise in writing.
Eligibility may depend on achievement of prescribed targets, successful joining, candidate/client continuation, revenue realization/collection, documentation, retention period and other conditions specified by the Company.
Incentives are discretionary and may be modified, suspended, withdrawn or discontinued by the Company based on business performance, revenue collection, financial circumstances, operational requirements or policy changes, subject to applicable law.
An incentive communicated or declared at one point in time shall not automatically create a permanent or vested entitlement for future periods.
6. WORKING HOURS AND WEEKLY OFF
Your normal working schedule shall be as prescribed by the Company for your department, office and designation.
The Company may modify working hours, shifts or schedules based on business requirements, subject to applicable law.
You shall be entitled to weekly rest days and applicable statutory holidays as prescribed by law and Company policy.
Where overtime is required and legally applicable, it shall be dealt with in accordance with applicable law and Company policy.
7. PROBATION
You shall initially be on probation for a period of three (3) months from your Date of Joining.
The probation period may be extended by the Company where required for performance assessment or other legitimate business reasons.
Confirmation of employment shall be communicated by the Company in writing.
Completion of the probation period shall not by itself constitute automatic confirmation unless confirmation is issued by the Company.
8. NOTICE PERIOD
During Probation
During probation, either party may terminate employment by providing [30 days] written notice or salary in lieu of notice, subject to applicable law and Company policy.
After Confirmation
After confirmation, either party shall provide [90 days] written notice or salary in lieu of notice, subject to applicable law and the terms approved by the Company.
The Company may, at its discretion, waive or reduce the notice period.
The employee shall not have an automatic right to adjust notice period against leave unless approved by the Company.
9. TERMINATION
The Company may terminate employment in accordance with applicable law and Company policy.
Termination may arise from, among other reasons:
Serious misconduct
Fraud, dishonesty or misrepresentation
Breach of confidentiality
Unauthorized disclosure of Company/client information
Theft or misuse of Company property
Serious violation of Company policies
Harassment or inappropriate workplace conduct
Falsification of documents, records or attendance
Unauthorized absence
Serious violation of information-security requirements
Persistent or unsatisfactory performance after appropriate review and opportunity for improvement, where applicable
Where disciplinary action is required, the Company shall follow the applicable disciplinary process and principles required by law.
Upon termination, the employee shall be entitled to salary and other statutory dues properly earned up to the last working day, subject to lawful deductions and applicable Company procedures.
10. ATTENDANCE AND PUNCTUALITY
Regular attendance and punctuality are essential requirements of employment.
You are required to:
Report to work on time.
Record attendance through the Company's designated system/ATS.
Obtain prior approval for planned leave or absence.
Follow office working hours and break schedules.
Inform the reporting manager promptly in case of emergency absence.
Unauthorized absence or repeated attendance violations may result in appropriate action under Company policy and applicable law.
11. LEAVE
Leave shall be governed by applicable labour laws and the Company's leave policy.
Employees shall be entitled to applicable statutory leave, public holidays, weekly holidays and other leave benefits as prescribed by law and Company policy.
Leave must normally be applied for and approved in advance, except in genuine emergencies.
12. EXCLUSIVITY OF EMPLOYMENT
During your employment, you shall devote your professional working time and attention to the Company's business.
You shall not undertake any employment, consultancy, freelance assignment, recruitment activity, business activity or other professional engagement that conflicts with your responsibilities or the Company's interests without prior written approval.
You shall not use Company resources, candidate databases, client information, ATS information or confidential information for outside employment or business.
13. CONFIDENTIALITY
During and after your employment, you shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding information relating to the Company, its clients, candidates, employees, vendors and business operations.
Confidential information includes, but is not limited to:
Client details
Candidate databases
Candidate resumes and personal information
Salary information
Recruitment processes
Business plans
Pricing and commercial information
Client requirements
Contracts and agreements
ATS data
Passwords and system access
Internal reports
Financial information
Employee information
Proprietary processes and documents
Such information shall not be disclosed, copied, transferred or used except for legitimate Company business.
14. DATA PROTECTION AND PRIVACY
You shall handle employee, candidate, client and business information responsibly and only for authorized business purposes.
You shall comply with applicable data-protection and privacy laws and the Company's information-security policies.
Candidate or client information shall not be downloaded, copied, transferred or stored on unauthorized personal devices, applications, email accounts or cloud services.
Any suspected data breach, unauthorized access or loss of information must be immediately reported to the Company.
15. ATS, EMAIL AND SYSTEM USAGE
Where applicable, you shall use the Company's designated ATS, email, communication systems and other technology platforms for official work.
All recruitment activities, candidate interactions, job submissions, client communications, interview updates, follow-ups and other required activities shall be recorded in the designated systems.
Employees shall not intentionally manipulate, falsify, delete or conceal system records.
Company systems may be monitored and audited in accordance with applicable law and Company policy.
16. COMPANY PROPERTY
All Company property provided to you shall remain the property of the Company.
This includes:
Laptop/computer
Mobile phone
SIM card
ID card
Access cards
Documents
Files
Software
ATS accounts
Email accounts
Databases
Recruitment portals
Login credentials
Other equipment or resources
All Company property must be returned immediately upon request or upon separation from employment.
17. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
Any work product, document, database, report, process, template, content, software-related material, recruitment material, business material or other intellectual property created by you during employment in connection with your duties shall belong to the Company to the extent permitted by applicable law.
You shall not copy, reproduce, sell, distribute or commercially use Company intellectual property without authorization.
18. BACKGROUND VERIFICATION
Your appointment is subject to satisfactory verification of information provided by you.
The Company may verify employment history, education, professional qualifications, references, identity and other information relevant to employment, subject to applicable law.
Any material misrepresentation, concealment or falsification may result in appropriate employment action.
19. CODE OF CONDUCT
You shall maintain professional and ethical conduct at all times.
You are expected to:
Treat colleagues, candidates, clients and business partners respectfully.
Maintain professional communication.
Follow Company policies and procedures.
Protect Company and client interests.
Avoid conflicts of interest.
Maintain confidentiality.
Follow workplace safety and security requirements.
The Company has zero tolerance for fraud, harassment, discrimination, intimidation, violence, serious misconduct or deliberate misuse of Company resources.
20. POSH AND WORKPLACE CONDUCT
The Company is committed to maintaining a safe and respectful workplace.
All employees are required to comply with applicable laws and Company policies relating to prevention of sexual harassment and workplace misconduct.
Complaints shall be handled through the Company's prescribed mechanism and applicable law.
21. TRANSFER AND BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS
Based on business requirements, the Company may transfer or assign you to another department, project, branch, office, client assignment or location, subject to applicable law and the terms of employment.
Such changes shall not ordinarily be treated as termination of employment.
22. COMPANY POLICIES
You shall comply with all applicable Company policies, SOPs, circulars, instructions and procedures issued from time to time.
These may include:
Attendance Policy
Leave Policy
Recruitment SOP
Performance Policy
Incentive Policy
Information Security Policy
Data Protection Policy
IT/ATS Usage Policy
Code of Conduct
POSH Policy
Asset Policy
Client Communication Policy
Disciplinary Policy
The Company may amend its policies from time to time based on business requirements and applicable law.
23. STATUTORY BENEFITS AND DEDUCTIONS
You shall receive statutory benefits and applicable protections in accordance with the laws applicable to your employment and eligibility.
Applicable statutory deductions may include Provident Fund, ESI, Professional Tax, TDS and other legally required deductions.
The Company's payroll shall be processed based on applicable statutory requirements and the Company's payroll policies.
24. DECLARATION BY EMPLOYEE
By accepting this appointment, you confirm that:
The information provided by you during recruitment is true and complete.
You have disclosed all material information relevant to your employment.
You have read and understood this appointment letter.
You agree to comply with Company policies and procedures.
You understand that targets and performance requirements may apply to your position.
You understand that incentives and variable payments are governed separately by Company policy and are not guaranteed salary.
You agree to maintain confidentiality and protect Company, client and candidate information.
You agree to use Company systems and resources only for authorized purposes.
You agree to comply with applicable laws and workplace requirements.
25. GOVERNING LAW
This appointment shall be governed by the laws applicable to the employment relationship in India and the applicable jurisdiction of the Company's place of employment, subject to applicable law.
26. ENTIRE UNDERSTANDING
This Master Offer & Appointment Letter, together with the applicable Salary Annexure, Role & KPI Annexure and Company policies, constitutes the understanding governing your employment.
If any provision of this letter conflicts with a mandatory provision of applicable law, the mandatory legal provision shall prevail to the extent of such conflict.
ACCEPTANCE OF APPOINTMENT
We welcome you to White Horse Manpower Consultancy Private Limited and look forward to your contribution to the Company's growth.
Please sign and return the acknowledgement confirming your acceptance of this appointment and its applicable annexures.

1. ROLE PURPOSE
The Branch / Team Manager is responsible for the overall operational performance of the assigned branch/team, including recruitment delivery, business development, employee productivity, client relationships, revenue generation, attendance, discipline, compliance and achievement of Company objectives.
The Manager is expected to take ownership of the branch/team and ensure that Company processes, targets and standards are followed.

The Manager shall be responsible for:
Overall day-to-day functioning of the assigned branch/team.
Ensuring the office is operational during scheduled working hours.
Ensuring adequate staffing and work allocation.
Monitoring employee attendance and punctuality.
Maintaining workplace discipline and professional conduct.
Ensuring proper use of Company systems and assets.
Escalating operational issues to management.
Ensuring Company SOPs are followed.
B. Recruitment Management
The Manager shall oversee:
Allocation of recruitment requirements.
Recruiter productivity.
Candidate sourcing and screening.
Quality of candidate submissions.
Interview coordination.
Offer follow-up.
Joining conversion.
Candidate retention.
Client recruitment requirements.
Recruitment team performance.
The Manager shall ensure that recruitment activity is focused on genuine and active client requirements.
C. Business Development

New client acquisition.
Existing client development.
Corporate relationship building.
Requirement generation.
Client meetings.
Empanelment.
Recruitment proposals.
Commercial coordination.
Revenue generation.
Payment/collection follow-up.
The Manager shall coordinate closely with the Business Development team.

Branch revenue

Business development

Your employment is performance-oriented.

Quality and quantity of work
Productivity
Attendance and punctuality

Timely completion of assigned work

Teamwork and professional conduct

5. INCENTIVES AND VARIABLE PAY
Any incentive, performance bonus, joining incentive, special incentive, commission or other variable payment shall be governed separately by the Company's applicable incentive policy.
Such payments are not part of guaranteed monthly salary unless specifically stated otherwise in writing.
Eligibility may depend on achievement of prescribed targets, successful joining, candidate/client continuation, revenue realization/collection, documentation, retention period and other conditions specified by the Company.
Incentives are discretionary and may be modified, suspended, withdrawn or discontinued by the Company based on business performance, revenue collection, financial circumstances, operational requirements or policy changes, subject to applicable law.

6. WORKING HOURS AND WEEKLY OFF
Your normal working schedule shall be as prescribed by the Company for your department, office and designation.
The Company may modify working hours, shifts or schedules based on business requirements, subject to applicable law.
You shall be entitled to weekly rest days and applicable statutory holidays as prescribed by law and Company policy.
Where overtime is required and legally applicable, it shall be dealt with in accordance with applicable law and Company policy.
7. PROBATION
You shall initially be on probation for a period of three (3) months from your Date of Joining.
The probation period may be extended by the Company where required for performance assessment or other legitimate business reasons.
Confirmation of employment shall be communicated by the Company in writing.
Completion of the probation period shall not by itself constitute automatic confirmation unless confirmation is issued by the Company.

During Probation

After Confirmation
After confirmation, either party shall provide [90 days] written notice or salary in lieu of notice, subject to applicable law and the terms approved by the Company.
The Company may, at its discretion, waive or reduce the notice period.
The employee shall not have an automatic right to adjust notice period against leave unless approved by the Company.
9. TERMINATION
The Company may terminate employment in accordance with applicable law and Company policy.
Termination may arise from, among other reasons:
Serious misconduct
Fraud, dishonesty or misrepresentation
Breach of confidentiality
Unauthorized disclosure of Company/client information
Theft or misuse of Company property
Serious violation of Company policies
Harassment or inappropriate workplace conduct
Falsification of documents, records or attendance
Unauthorized absence
Serious violation of information-security requirements
Persistent or unsatisfactory performance after appropriate review and opportunity for improvement, where applicable
Where disciplinary action is required, the Company shall follow the applicable disciplinary process and principles required by law.
Upon termination, the employee shall be entitled to salary and other statutory dues properly earned up to the last working day, subject to lawful deductions and applicable Company procedures.
10. ATTENDANCE AND PUNCTUALITY
Regular attendance and punctuality are essential requirements of employment.
You are required to:
Report to work on time.
Record attendance through the Company's designated system/ATS.
Obtain prior approval for planned leave or absence.
Follow office working hours and break schedules.
Inform the reporting manager promptly in case of emergency absence.
Unauthorized absence or repeated attendance violations may result in appropriate action under Company policy and applicable law.
11. LEAVE
Leave shall be governed by applicable labour laws and the Company's leave policy.
Employees shall be entitled to applicable statutory leave, public holidays, weekly holidays and other leave benefits as prescribed by law and Company policy.
Leave must normally be applied for and approved in advance, except in genuine emergencies.
12. EXCLUSIVITY OF EMPLOYMENT
During your employment, you shall devote your professional working time and attention to the Company's business.
You shall not undertake any employment, consultancy, freelance assignment, recruitment activity, business activity or other professional engagement that conflicts with your responsibilities or the Company's interests without prior written approval.
You shall not use Company resources, candidate databases, client information, ATS information or confidential information for outside employment or business.
13. CONFIDENTIALITY
During and after your employment, you shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding information relating to the Company, its clients, candidates, employees, vendors and business operations.

Client details
Candidate databases
Candidate resumes and personal information
Salary information
Recruitment processes
Business plans
Pricing and commercial information
Client requirements
Contracts and agreements
ATS data
Passwords and system access
Internal reports
Financial information
Employee information
Proprietary processes and documents
Such information shall not be disclosed, copied, transferred or used except for legitimate Company business.
14. DATA PROTECTION AND PRIVACY
You shall handle employee, candidate, client and business information responsibly and only for authorized business purposes.
You shall comply with applicable data-protection and privacy laws and the Company's information-security policies.
Candidate or client information shall not be downloaded, copied, transferred or stored on unauthorized personal devices, applications, email accounts or cloud services.
Any suspected data breach, unauthorized access or loss of information must be immediately reported to the Company.
15. ATS, EMAIL AND SYSTEM USAGE
Where applicable, you shall use the Company's designated ATS, email, communication systems and other technology platforms for official work.
All recruitment activities, candidate interactions, job submissions, client communications, interview updates, follow-ups and other required activities shall be recorded in the designated systems.
Employees shall not intentionally manipulate, falsify, delete or conceal system records.
Company systems may be monitored and audited in accordance with applicable law and Company policy.

Other equipment or resources
All Company property must be returned immediately upon request or upon separation from employment.
17. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
Any work product, document, database, report, process, template, content, software-related material, recruitment material, business material or other intellectual property created by you during employment in connection with your duties shall belong to the Company to the extent permitted by applicable law.
You shall not copy, reproduce, sell, distribute or commercially use Company intellectual property without authorization.
18. BACKGROUND VERIFICATION
Your appointment is subject to satisfactory verification of information provided by you.
The Company may verify employment history, education, professional qualifications, references, identity and other information relevant to employment, subject to applicable law.
Any material misrepresentation, concealment or falsification may result in appropriate employment action.
19. CODE OF CONDUCT
You shall maintain professional and ethical conduct at all times.
You are expected to:
Treat colleagues, candidates, clients and business partners respectfully.
Maintain professional communication.
Follow Company policies and procedures.
Protect Company and client interests.
Avoid conflicts of interest.
Maintain confidentiality.
Follow workplace safety and security requirements.
The Company has zero tolerance for fraud, harassment, discrimination, intimidation, violence, serious misconduct or deliberate misuse of Company resources.
20. POSH AND WORKPLACE CONDUCT
The Company is committed to maintaining a safe and respectful workplace.
All employees are required to comply with applicable laws and Company policies relating to prevention of sexual harassment and workplace misconduct.
Complaints shall be handled through the Company's prescribed mechanism and applicable law.
21. TRANSFER AND BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS
Based on business requirements, the Company may transfer or assign you to another department, project, branch, office, client assignment or location, subject to applicable law and the terms of employment.
Such changes shall not ordinarily be treated as termination of employment.
22. COMPANY POLICIES
You shall comply with all applicable Company policies, SOPs, circulars, instructions and procedures issued from time to time.

Applicable statutory deductions may include Provident Fund, ESI, Professional Tax, TDS and other legally required deductions.
The Company's payroll shall be processed based on applicable statutory requirements and the Company's payroll policies.
24. DECLARATION BY EMPLOYEE
By accepting this appointment, you confirm that:
The information provided by you during recruitment is true and complete.
You have disclosed all material information relevant to your employment.
You have read and understood this appointment letter.
You agree to comply with Company policies and procedures.

You understand that incentives and variable payments are governed separately by Company policy and are not guaranteed salary.
You agree to maintain confidentiality and protect Company, client and candidate information.
You agree to use Company systems and resources only for authorized purposes.
You agree to comply with applicable laws and workplace requirements.
25. GOVERNING LAW
This appointment shall be governed by the laws applicable to the employment relationship in India and the applicable jurisdiction of the Company's place of employment, subject to applicable law.
26. ENTIRE UNDERSTANDING
This Master Offer & Appointment Letter, together with the applicable Salary Annexure, Role & KPI Annexure and Company policies, constitutes the understanding governing your employment.
If any provision of this letter conflicts with a mandatory provision of applicable law, the mandatory legal provision shall prevail to the extent of such conflict.

Theft or misuse of Company property
Serious violation of Company policies
